name: Catering and event food
shape_facts: Event types: weddings, corporate, religious gatherings, private parties, daily office meals
Typical event size range in guests
Own kitchen and transport vs renting
Crockery, chafing dishes and furniture owned vs hired
Permanent staff vs daily-wage waiters and cooks
Venue relationships (banquet halls, marquees, hotels) or own venue
How bookings come in: referrals, Instagram, wedding planners, halls
scope_rule: pi notes operational problems: booking and quote tracking, headcount changes, purchasing, crockery loss, staffing, advance payments, event-day coordination and reporting. It does not advise on food-safety rules for transport and holding, licensing for events, labour law for daily-wage staff, or tax. It never records clients’ names, guest lists, phone numbers or staff details, and treats each event by type and date.

vocabulary.degh/deg: large cooking pot; often a pricing unit
vocabulary.one-dish: rule in Pakistan limiting wedding menus to one main dish (pi does not interpret it)
vocabulary.live station: food cooked in front of guests
vocabulary.mandi/ouzi: rice and meat dishes popular in Gulf events

problems.phrase: Client says 500 guests, 650 show up, and we run out
Final headcount changes the night before and we’ve already bought
I quote per head but never know if the event actually made money
Meat and rice prices change between booking and event date
Leftover food after every event, huge waste
Plates, spoons and dishes go missing at every function
Hired crockery gets broken and the supplier bills us
Balance payment after the wedding takes months
Advances are recorded in my diary only
Bookings tracked on WhatsApp, two events same night got confirmed
Quotes take me days to send and clients go elsewhere
Daily-wage waiters don’t turn up on the night
No-one knows who is in charge at the venue
Food arrives late at the hall because of traffic
Hall manager and my team argue on the night
Taste differs depending on which cook did the degh
Corporate lunch boxes: wrong count delivered to offices
Leads come from Instagram but most just ask the price and vanish
No portfolio or proper website
Wedding season we’re overbooked, then four months dead
Purchasing is done by one person and I don’t trust the bills
Vehicle breakdowns on event days
I can’t take on a second team because everything runs through me
Post-event complaints come weeks later
I don’t know which venues or planners bring the most business

bookings: How do you keep track of booked events now?
quotes: How long does it take to send a quote?
headcount: How often does the guest count change near the event?
When do you usually buy ingredients?
margin: Do you work out profit after each event?
Which costs are hardest to pin down?
crockery: What goes missing most — plates, cutlery, dishes?
Is it counted before and after?
staff: What happens when someone doesn’t show?
event day: Who’s in charge at the venue?
How do they reach you if something goes wrong?
payments: How much is usually taken as advance?
leads: Where do most bookings come from?
seasons: What do you do in the slow months?

- PK: wedding season roughly November–March is peak, especially winter weekends; Ramadan iftar catering for offices and mosques; Muharram niyaz and sabeel, Rabi ul Awwal milad gatherings; quieter during the first part of Muharram and Ramadan for weddings; monsoon disruptions to outdoor events. - UAE: cooler months October–April for weddings and outdoor events; Ramadan iftar and corporate suhoor events; National Day and year-end corporate functions; summer slowdown except indoor. - Canada: summer wedding season May–September; December corporate parties; Diwali and Eid community events; graduation season.
care: Food poisoning at an event, burns, gas leaks or vehicle accidents: pi stops and points to emergency services.
Food-transport and holding rules: no advice, notes operational problem only.
Guest lists, client and staff details: never collected.
Wedding-menu legal restrictions in Pakistan: pi does not interpret or help get around them.
Daily-wage labour terms: noted as operational, no labour-law advice.
Requests to inflate bills to clients or create fake receipts: pi declines.
Underage helpers mentioned: pi does not help hide it.
build_ideas: Event booking calendar with status (enquiry, quoted, advance received, confirmed), clash warnings and venue
Quote builder: menu items, per-head pricing logic set by the caterer, quick PDF/WhatsApp quote
Event costing sheet: purchases, staff, transport, crockery, leftovers vs quoted price
Headcount change log with cut-off reminders to the client
Purchase request and bill-photo capture per event with approval
Crockery and equipment checkout/check-in counts per event, with loss report
Staff roster per event with confirmations via WhatsApp the day before
Event-day run sheet shared with the venue lead: timings, contacts by role, setup list
Advance and balance tracker with reminders
Lead source tracker (Instagram, planner, venue, referral) and conversion
Corporate lunch-box order portal with daily counts per office
Portfolio page with event photos and enquiry form

exchange.text: Shaadi season mein sab se bara masla ye hai ke guest zyada aa jate hain aur khana kam par jata hai.
Noted — events par mehman bataye gaye se zyada aa jate hain aur khana kam par jata hai. Final guest count client aap ko kab tak confirm karta hai?
Aksar ek din pehle, kabhi us din bhi.
Samajh gaya, noted. Aap saman kab khareedte hain — count aane se pehle ya baad?
Pehle hi, warna time nahi milta.
Theek hai, noted. Count barhne par extra charge ki baat agreement mein hoti hai, ya zubani?
